QE-R7ASE-01.finding: When the athlete lifts a projected load, atDose (src/r6-adaptation.mjs:714-720) promotes the stored start's whole dose, including the load tick. When the projection ran two weeks ahead of history, the tick at the new load counts an exposure never executed. Identical ledgers: U db-rdl and db-split-squat KNOWN 24 tick 1 (basis WEEK_EVIDENCE week 8, rebuilt) against R6 tick 0; after a SHORT return U steps to 26 kg on 2027-01-09, R6 on 2027-01-16. The SSCTR independently reports the same atom (NF-R7ASE-3, back squat) and does not approve it as history
QE-R7ASE-01.reproduction: reviews/qe-r7ase-P51d-identical-ledgers.mjs; reviews/qe-r7ase-P51c-atdose-projected-tick-unmet.mjs (four time zones and the boundary copy); reviews/qe-r7ase-P51b-atdose-projected-tick-dev.mjs; reviews/ssctr-r7ase-tick-probe.mjs
QE-R7ASE-01.stateAtomThatLostProvenance: A strength exercise's loadTick (the count of successful exposures at the current load): recorded basis WEEK_EVIDENCE rebuilt, real provenance a CONDITIONAL_PLAN's assumption about a missed session. By the same code also the repetition target under a repetition-progression goal (the judge: inferred, not run)
QE-R7ASE-01.fromChosenGranularity: Yes. One strength exercise is one value (contract §3); atDose promotes the value's whole dose tuple on the evidence of one of its atoms (the load), a container-level promotion inside the value
QE-R7ASE-01.physicalSeparationOfHistoricalStateAndPl: Not required for this instance: promoting only the load and deriving the tick from executed exposures would close it (SSCTR R42). The engineering judge reads the pattern as an argument for it: history is rebuilt by copying values out of the planning record under per-value rules, and two such copy rules have now leaked (QE-R7AB-01, then this one, introduced by its fix). A HistoricalState advanced only by executed evidence would remove the class structurally

QE-R7ASE-02.finding: The planner's D52 predicate needsReestablishment (src/r6-program.mjs:335, used at :362; 'in calendar days from its last executed exposure') reads lastPerformed from the planning start. A review updates that date only for an exercise performed in its week, so a planned date carried from an unreviewed week survives every later review in which the exercise is missed. In P40's U: planning 2026-11-21 (never executed), history 2026-11-14; on 2026-12-19, 35 days after the last exposure, U prescribes db-rdl 3x5@3 KNOWN 22 and db-split-squat 2x6@3 KNOWN 22, never lifted, where R prescribes the D52 re-establishment by effort. Same class (P52): return-step doses planned from a projected return step after the re-entry session was missed
QE-R7ASE-02.reproduction: reviews/qe-r7ase-P50-reestablish-projected-date.mjs (four time zones and the boundary copy); reviews/qe-r7ase-I02-same-facts.mjs; reviews/qe-r7ase-P52-fresh-exercise-entryweek.mjs
QE-R7ASE-02.stateAtomThatLostProvenance: A strength exercise's lastPerformed in the planning view (stateTrace[k].strength.exercises[id].lastPerformed), read as the last executed exposure; in P52 the exercises' returnStep, read by the row's exposure kind
QE-R7ASE-02.fromChosenGranularity: No. The value is correctly identified (projectedBase) and history is right; the planner evaluates a predicate defined on executed history against the planning view (contract E1 too broad: 'the next review reads the facts' is false for atoms a review does not move)
QE-R7ASE-02.physicalSeparationOfHistoricalStateAndPl: Separate read paths are required: history-defined predicates inside the planner must read the historical view. Physical separation is one way to enforce it, not the only one; one record serving both views is what lets such a predicate silently read a projected atom (the judge)
